name: Aram
overview: Aram is a male biblical figure identified as the son of Shem, as recorded in Genesis 10:22. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His primary distinction in Scripture is his lineage as a descendant of Shem.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Aram' appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:22 without any given meaning or divine attribution. It is presented simply as the personal name of this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Aram is explicitly noted as the son of Shem. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash according to Genesis 10:23. These relationships establish him as a patriarchal figure within his family line.
scriptureSignificance: Aram's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a direct descendant of Shem, situating him within the genealogical framework that traces the origins of various peoples. As the father of several sons, he contributes to the unfolding of nations descending from Shem, which is important for understanding the biblical ethnology. His mention underscores God's providential ordering of human history through chosen lineages.
